observations.description: Original 3D cartoon animation in the same character style; an economics explainer told through a metaphor (eggs and chickens) with diagrams drawn inside the scene (chalkboard '2 = egg').
Visible dissolves between scenes (ghosted double images) and heavy horizontal motion blur on fast camera moves.
Story text appears as in-scene signs ('UNFAIR!', 'BOO!', 'WE WANT EGGS') rather than overlay graphics.

Captions show 1-2 words at a time in sentence case with punctuation kept (e.g. 'Wait,', 'paradise.'); white heavy rounded sans-serif with a thin dark outline and soft shadow, centred just below the middle of the frame. No boxes, no emoji.
Font category: heavy geometric/rounded sans-serif (Poppins/Montserrat-like category). The exact font cannot be identified from the frames.
Question hook, metaphor-driven explanation, and an ending that loops back to the three groups named at the start.
Hook is a single concrete paradox stated immediately: "Why do the rich keep getting richer while the poor get poorer?"
Ends on a concrete payoff that resolves the hook, no call to action: "The poor, the middle class, and the rich."

categorical.hook_style: one-sentence concrete paradox (strange action, absurd consequence, or rule + contradiction), no intro
categorical.ending_style: concrete payoff image that resolves the hook, then the video stops (no CTA, no summary)
